Hi Sam — thanks for the note and timeline. Happy to run the kickoff next week. Initial answers up front:

- Default recommendation: US‑East (us-east1) for lowest latency to your east‑coast user base; EU‑West as standby region for failover.
- We can provision a short burst window for turnup (policy options below) — need to confirm expected sustained and peak TPS to size burst credits.
- For private deployments we will need your VPC peering details, KMS/secret access policy, and a list of subnets for the control plane.

To size the pool precisely please send: average QPS, 95th p95 latency target, typical sequence length, and model family(s) (e.g., Llama‑style 7B float16, or Llama2 70B quantized).

Proposed next steps:
1) Kickoff meeting (30m) to capture requirements — I’ll propose time slots.
2) Rishi will run a quick capacity estimate template (I’ve CC’d him).
3) Draft SOW & activation checklist from our side (Monica will own).

Available slots: Tue 6/20 10:00-11:00 PT, Wed 6/21 14:00-15:00 PT. Which works?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for model inference: timeline & regional question

Hi all — looping in a quick technical sketch while we wait on the kickoff slot.

Quick assumptions: 7B–13B family for conversational features, expected average seq length 128 tokens, peaks up to 512 tokens, target p95 generation latency <= 350ms.

Suggested baseline pool:
- GPUs: 8 x A100‑40GB for warm pool (sustained throughput); 2 x A100‑80GB as cold spare for large/long sequences.
- Autoscale policy: target CPU/GPU util band 45%–70%; scale step: add 1 GPU per 60s when queue > threshold.
- Burst policy options:
  • Short burst (recommended): allow +30% capacity for 72 hours using reserved spare capacity — subject to credit usage.
  • Extended burst: +60% for 24 hours with pre‑purchase commit (discounted).
- Caching: enable prefix KV cache for repeated prompts (reduces token forward comps); configure 24h KV TTL for session affinity.

I attached a capacity‑estimate template; please drop your QPS figures and model mix and I’ll produce a cost/latency tradeoff matrix.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: capacity-estimate-template.xlsx]

Thanks Rishi — attaching our informal load snapshot. Short answers:

- Average QPS (inference requests): 65
- Peak QPS: 420 (short spikes during campaign windows)
- Typical sequence length: 160 tokens; heavy jobs up to 600 tokens.
- Model family: mix of 13B quantized Llama‑style for production and 70B for occasional high‑quality jobs.

Primary region: US‑East (us-east1). EU‑West as backup — we’d like an automated failover plan.

Request: Can you confirm a 72‑hour burst at +40% (not +30%)? For our opening campaign we need some headroom. Also please include a rough cost delta for the burst window.

Sam

Thanks for the numbers. Attached is a draft SOW and an activation checklist. Highlights:

- Milestone 1 (Provisioning): Reserve 8 A100‑40GB nodes in us‑east1 + 2 A100‑80GB cold spares. Target complete: 2028‑06‑28.

- Milestone 3 (Go‑Live & Burst): Enable +40% burst credits for 72h window starting at go‑live; cost estimate included in SOW appendix.

2) Provide VPC peering CIDR blocks and KMS IAM role for provisioning.
